title: The survivors return
summary: After burying the dead, the surviving Nephites returned to their lands and homes, to their wives and children.

explicit_facts.text: The surviving Nephites buried the slain and returned to their lands, houses, wives, and children.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Survivors arrive at their homes after the burials.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the homes and the identities of the survivors and families.

narration.text: after they had finished burying their dead
they all returned to their lands, and to their houses

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an earlier burial scene; it is reported as already completed.

title: The battle’s losses
summary: Women, children, flocks, herds, and grain fields had been lost or destroyed. Slain Lamanites and Amlicites from the bank of the Sidon were cast into the river.

explicit_facts.text: Many women and children had been slain, and many flocks, herds, and grain fields were destroyed.
Slain Lamanites and Amlicites on the bank of the Sidon were cast into its waters.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The riverbank and water can be shown with the aftermath of battle, without graphic detail.
unspecified_visual_details: Who cast the slain into the river; the number and appearance of the people, animals, and fields.

narration.text: many women and children had been slain with the sword
the Lamanites and the Amlicites who had been slain upon the bank of the river Sidon were cast into the waters of Sidon

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the deaths as occurring now; they are reported aftermath.

title: Marks and clothing described
summary: The narrator describes distinguishing marks and appearance: Amlicites marked their foreheads red and did not shave their heads like the Lamanites; Lamanite heads were shorn, and they wore loin coverings and armor and carried weapons.

explicit_facts.text: Amlicites marked their foreheads red and did not shave their heads like the Lamanites.
Lamanites had shorn heads, loin coverings, armor, bows, arrows, stones, and slings.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A neutral, non-event portrait may show the described differences.
unspecified_visual_details: Exact hairstyles, armor, weapons’ design, and the appearance of individuals.

narration.text: they had marked themselves with red in their foreheads
the heads of the Lamanites were shorn

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses describe reported distinguishing features, not a new present-tense action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign the described skin color in verse 6 to any present-day ethnic group or treat it as a visual cue beyond what the text explicitly states.

title: The account of the mark
summary: The narrator relates the mark placed upon Laman, Lemuel, the sons of Ishmael, and Ishmaelitish women, and explains its intended distinction between their descendants and their brethren’s descendants.

explicit_facts.text: The account says a mark was set upon Laman, Lemuel, the sons of Ishmael, and Ishmaelitish women.
The stated purpose was to distinguish their seed from their brethren’s seed and preserve the Lord’s people from mixing and incorrect traditions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This is narration about past events and stated purpose; no historical figures need appear in the present scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The mark’s appearance and any depiction of historical individuals.

narration.text: the Lord God set a mark upon them
that their seed might be distinguished from the seed of their brethren

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 6 includes a doctrinal claim about the mark; it is reported narration, not a separate visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not visually invent a divine appearance or depict ancestors as present.

title: Mingling and allegiance
summary: The narrator states that mingling with the Lamanites brought the same curse upon a person’s seed, and that one led away by the Lamanites was called under that name and marked.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator says that one who mingled his seed with the Lamanites brought the same curse upon his seed.
One led away by the Lamanites was called under that head and had a mark set upon him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The passage is a general statement and does not establish a specific person or occasion to depict.
unspecified_visual_details: Any individuals, location, or appearance of the mark.

narration.text: whosoever did mingle his seed with that of the Lamanites
there was a mark set upon him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: General narration, not a narrated particular event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an invented person receiving a mark.

title: Those called Nephites
summary: Those who rejected Lamanite tradition, believed the records from Jerusalem and their fathers’ correct tradition, and kept God’s commandments were called Nephites; they kept records of both peoples.

explicit_facts.text: Those described as believing the records from Jerusalem and correct traditions and keeping God’s commandments were called Nephites.
They kept true records of their people and the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The records may be represented as written records, but their physical form is unspecified.
unspecified_visual_details: Any record-keepers, writing materials, or setting.

narration.text: were called the Nephites, or the people of Nephi
they who have kept the records which are true of their people

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent visible record-keepers or a specific record-making scene.

title: The Amlicites’ red marks
summary: The narrator returns to the Amlicites, who set a red mark upon their own foreheads.

explicit_facts.text: The Amlicites set a red mark upon their own foreheads.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group of Amlicites may be shown marking their foreheads.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, marking implement, and exact appearance of the mark.

narration.text: they set the mark upon themselves
even a mark of red upon their foreheads

prohibited_inventions: Do not give the Amlicites names or individual biographies.

title: Words spoken to Nephi
summary: The narrator quotes promises concerning marks, separation, repentance, mercy, and the seed of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator says these words were spoken to Nephi and quotes promises concerning the Lamanites, those who mingle with them, those who fight Nephi’s seed, and those who depart from it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration; the quoted address does not describe a visible speaker or setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Who is visibly speaking, where the words were spoken, and the historical moment.

narration.text: Behold, the Lamanites have I cursed
except they repent of their wickedness
I will set a mark upon him that mingleth his seed with thy brethren
I will set a mark upon him that fighteth against thee and thy seed
I will bless thee

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chapter presents these as quotations of words spoken to Nephi; it does not narrate their delivery as a present visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God or Nephi as physically present in an invented setting.

title: Amlicite rebellion and condemnation
summary: The Amlicites did not know they were fulfilling God’s words when they marked themselves; the narrator says they had rebelled against God and brought the curse and condemnation upon themselves.

explicit_facts.text: The Amlicites marked their foreheads without knowing they were fulfilling God’s words and had openly rebelled against God.
The narrator says they brought the curse upon themselves and that a cursed person brings his own condemnation upon himself.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This may be conveyed with the Amlicites’ already-described red forehead marks; the condemnation is an explanatory teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: Any specific act beyond marking, and any visible form of curse or condemnation.

narration.text: they had come out in open rebellion against God
they brought upon themselves the curse

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not literalize the curse or condemnation as a visible supernatural effect.

title: A new Lamanite army
summary: Not many days after the battle in Zarahemla, another Lamanite army came upon the people of Nephi at the same place as the earlier encounter; an army was sent to drive them out.

explicit_facts.text: Another Lamanite army came upon the people of Nephi at the place where the first army met the Amlicites.
An army was sent to drive the Lamanites out of their land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The opposing armies may be shown confronting one another at the reported location.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact site, army sizes, commanders, and formations.

narration.text: there was another army of the Lamanites came in upon the people of Nephi
there was an army sent to drive them out of their land

prohibited_inventions: Do not place Alma in the battle; the following verse says he did not go.

title: Alma stays behind
summary: Alma, afflicted with a wound, did not go up to battle against the Lamanites at this time.

explicit_facts.text: Alma was afflicted with a wound and did not go to battle at this time.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown apart from the battle, with no graphic wound depiction.
unspecified_visual_details: The wound’s location and appearance, Alma’s precise location, and his activity.

narration.text: Alma himself being afflicted with a wound
did not go up to battle at this time

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the wound graphically or invent how it occurred.

title: The Lamanites driven out
summary: A numerous Nephite army went against the Lamanites, slew many, and drove the remainder out of the borders of their land.

explicit_facts.text: A numerous army slew many Lamanites and drove the rest beyond the borders of the Nephite land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fighting and retreat may be shown without graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: Commanders, the precise battlefield, and the armies’ appearance.

narration.text: they went up and slew many of the Lamanites
drove the remainder of them out of the borders of their land

prohibited_inventions: Do not show wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Peace for a time
summary: The Nephite army returned, and peace began to be established in the land; the people were troubled no more for a time by their enemies.

explicit_facts.text: The army returned and began to establish peace; the people were not troubled by enemies for a time.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The returning army may be shown after the fighting, without suggesting a specific peace ceremony.
unspecified_visual_details: How peace was established and the appearance of the land.

narration.text: they returned again and began to establish peace in the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a treaty, celebration, or political gathering.

title: The fifth year’s toll
summary: The narrator states that the wars and contentions began and ended in the fifth year of the judges, and that thousands and tens of thousands died in that year and received rewards according to their works.

explicit_facts.text: All the wars and contentions described were commenced and ended in the fifth year of the judges.
Thousands and tens of thousands were sent to the eternal world and reaped rewards according to their works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This is a summary and teaching, not a new battle or a visible afterlife scene.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visual depiction of the eternal world, the dead, or their rewards.

narration.text: all these wars and contentions were commenced and ended in the fifth year of the reign of the judges
thousands and tens of thousands of souls

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The eternal rewards and miseries are stated teaching; do not depict them as visible events.
prohibited_inventions: No invented afterlife imagery, spirits, or judgment scene.

title: The fifth year ends
summary: The narrator teaches that each person receives wages from the one they choose to obey, according to the prophetic word, and concludes the fifth year of the judges.

explicit_facts.text: Each person receives wages from the one they choose to obey, according to the word of prophecy.
The fifth year of the reign of the judges ended.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A neutral closing image may accompany off-screen narration; the verse specifies no visible event.
unspecified_visual_details: Any people, setting, or visual form of the wages.

narration.text: every man receiveth wages of him whom he listeth to obey
And thus endeth the fifth year of the reign of the judges.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wages are figurative teaching, not a literal visible transaction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal payment or an invented scene.
